Based on what's been retrieved, no — we don't have a genuinely comparable precedent for this case. Case_007 is a clean, textbook round-tripping pattern: a 5-account closed loop (ACCT-2054→2055→2056→2057→2058→2054), all hops within 24 hours, amounts consistent within ~5% ($25,068–$26,722), and every account alerted for circular fund flow. All three standardized round_tripping criteria (RT-1 cyclical flow, RT-2 tight timing, RT-3 similar amounts with no apparent economic purpose) are matched with no mitigating explanation on file — KYC notes are blank for all five accounts.

None of the three retrieved precedents match this typology or fact pattern closely:
- case_005 is a mule_hub fan-out case (20 counterparties), not a cycle, and was closed after the account holder's marketplace-seller activity was corroborated — a different structure and a different resolution path (legitimate business explanation).
- case_001 is a structuring/layering case (12 near-threshold deposits into one hub account, then consolidated outflow) — it does share the "escalate due to timing/pattern despite plausible partial explanation" logic, but the underlying pattern (fan-in/threshold evasion) is structurally different from a closed circular loop, and it also had a partial legitimate business explanation (invoiced catering payments) that case_007 lacks entirely.
- case_013 is a single transaction between two long-tenured, income-consistent accounts with no red flags — essentially the opposite pattern from a 5-hop cycle with fresh KYC gaps and short tenure on some accounts.

So while case_001 offers a loose analogy in that both involve multi-account layering patterns escalated despite an available account narrative, none of the precedents describe a matching round-tripping cycle. I'd treat case_007 as either a first-of-its-kind for this checklist or note that our precedent set simply doesn't yet contain a true round-tripping comparator — worth flagging that gap rather than forcing an analogy.

citations.note: Closest structural analogy: multi-account layering pattern escalated based on timing/amount clustering despite a partially plausible business explanation, though the topology (fan-in/threshold evasion) differs from case_007's closed cycle.
Different typology (mule_hub fan-out) and was resolved via corroborated legitimate business activity — contrasts with case_007's lack of any KYC explanation.
Single clean transaction between long-tenured accounts with no anomalies — illustrates the opposite end of the risk spectrum from case_007's 5-hop circular flow.
